text: But it is possible. What happen? In other cases, the coordinator remains awake, and sensors may go to sleep. Okay, so in that case, clearly they will not be able to transmit or receive traffic. Clearly, during these time intervals in which sensors are asleep, if the coordinator gets some traffic to be delivered to them, the coordinator needs to store cache these packets, wait for the sensors to wake up, and then he will be able to deliver the packets to the sensors. So from that we understand that the role of the coordinator is quite heavy. First of all, because well sometimes it can go to sleep as well, but that means that the whole network will go to sleep. Otherwise, the coordinator needs to remain awake, and then if the sensors, the single sensors, go to sleep, the coordinator needs to store packets for them. So if the sensors go to sleep for a long time, well then that's also something challenging because the coordinator is still a sensor with reduced capabilities. So if it has to store many packets, then that's an issue. Okay, after a while, it may actually need to drop some packets because.
